supporting_observations.claim: The repeated HTTPS-related activity is consistent with the approved ChartMate updater: cmupdate.exe ran on WS-BCARTER-01 and connected through the proxy to update.chartmate-imaging.com:443 at roughly five-minute intervals, including 13:41, 13:46, 13:51, 13:56, 14:01, 14:06, and 14:10 UTC.

At 13:20 UTC, Kerberos requests from WS-BCARTER-01 used lucy.park's account for a service ticket to WS-LPARK-01, followed by a network logon for lucy.park on WS-LPARK-01 from WS-BCARTER-01's IP. This is unexplained by the supplied remote-administration practice, but the records alone do not establish why it occurred.
A UserAssist registry entry records a path that decodes to powershell.exe for ben.carter, but the supplied records do not show a corresponding PowerShell process start or its command line.

Cisco AnyConnect's UI launched on WS-BCARTER-01, and shortly afterward the proxy recorded a connection to downloads.cloud.com. The supplied inventory says there is no VPN and no other approved cloud-storage or file-sharing service; these records do not establish that a VPN connected or that a file was transferred.
An SMB connection from WS-BCARTER-01 to DC-HD-01 was accompanied by an ANONYMOUS LOGON network logon. The evidence does not identify the share or SMB operation, so its significance is unclear.
The evidence also shows a proxy connection to dellupdater.dell.com with a Dell Command Update user agent; it does not identify a suspicious payload or outcome.

known_telemetry_limitations: The ChartMate HTTPS sessions are represented as proxy CONNECT tunnels; the supplied records identify the destination and traffic sizes but do not expose the TLS contents. (T026-00095, T026-00120, T026-00150, T026-00167, T026-00197)
The PowerShell-related evidence is a UserAssist registry entry only; no corresponding process-start record or command line is present in the supplied evidence. (T026-00137)

The records show the AnyConnect UI launch but no VPN tunnel establishment, and show a connection to downloads.cloud.com without identifying a downloaded file or its contents. (T026-00221, T026-00223, T026-00236, T026-00237)
The SMB records do not show the share name or file and command activity associated with the anonymous network logon. (T026-00158, T026-00161, T026-00162)
claims_not_established: Whether lucy.park's authentication from WS-BCARTER-01 to WS-LPARK-01 was authorized or involved credential misuse. (T026-00021, T026-00024)
Whether PowerShell was actually executed during the review window, and, if so, what it did. (T026-00137)
Whether AnyConnect established a VPN connection or downloads.cloud.com was used to transfer an unapproved file. (T026-00221, T026-00236, T026-00237)
Whether the anonymous SMB session to DC-HD-01 accessed any resource or performed any action. (T026-00158, T026-00161, T026-00162)
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve process-creation and PowerShell operational/script-block logs for WS-BCARTER-01 around 13:20–14:20 UTC, including command lines and parent processes.
Review WS-LPARK-01 authentication and endpoint records around 13:20 UTC, plus account-use records for lucy.park, to determine the purpose and authorization of the network logon.
Check VPN client and network gateway logs to determine whether AnyConnect established a tunnel.
Obtain proxy or endpoint download details for downloads.cloud.com, including the initiating process, URL/path, file metadata, and disposition.
Review SMB server/share auditing on DC-HD-01 around 13:58:59 UTC to identify the resource and operations associated with the anonymous session.
